title: envtally config
description: Any key that starts with .comment is a note for people and is ignored, in every object.

defaults.description: Global settings. Command-line flags override them.

profile.description: Profile for apps that do not set one. Built in: springboot, rails, flask.

retries.description: Retries when no HTTP response arrives (connection error, timeout). An HTTP response, 5xx included, is never retried.

slowThreshold.description: Instances whose total response time exceeds this are marked slow.

envOrder.description: Display order of envs, e.g. ["dev", "test", "prod"]. Envs not listed follow in alphabetical order.

vars.description: Literal values usable as ${name} in link templates and header values.

profiles.description: App types. A profile named springboot, rails or flask replaces the built-in one.

comment.description: A note for people. envtally ignores it. One string, or an array of strings for several lines.

templates.description: Named links printed by `envtally urls`, e.g. swagger and jenkins. Each is a pattern or a literal URL. Variables: ${project} ${app} ${env} ${host} ${base_url} and anything in vars. Override order: global, then project, then app.

healthPath.description: Path appended to the instance URL. Healthy = HTTP 2xx (and healthyWhen, if set). The body can be anything unless healthyWhen or groupKey reads it.

infoPath.description: Optional second endpoint, called when health passed. It must answer HTTP 2xx. With a groupKey, the key is built from its JSON (without infoPath, from the health JSON).

healthyWhen.description: Also require a field of the health JSON to equal a value.

groupKey.description: Optional. Template of dot-paths into the response JSON, e.g. ${build.version}|${git.commit.id}. A missing field renders as ? and marks the env UNKNOWN. Leave it out for a status-only profile: HTTP 2xx means UP and no versions are compared (for apps without a JSON version endpoint, such as Jenkins).

headers.description: HTTP request headers sent with every health and info request of this profile: header name -> value. In a value, ${env:NAME} is replaced by the OS environment variable NAME (use it for secrets) and ${name} by a value from vars. Example: { "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:API_TOKEN}" }, after `export API_TOKEN=...` (bash) or `$env:API_TOKEN = "..."` (PowerShell).

profile.description: Profile name. Falls back to defaults.profile.

envs.description: Env name -> instance URL, or an array of instance URLs.

url.description: Instance base URL (http or https, no query or fragment).
